H6WY01173.name: Lisa Kinney
H6WY01173.bio: Former Wyoming state senator (1985-1995) and minority floor leader; former financial advisor, Albany County Library director and Laramie Area Chamber of Commerce president.

positions.stance: "Public lands belong in public hands. We cannot give them away or sell them."
Wants Congress to exercise its constitutional checks and balances, with "No relinquishing power to the President."
Calls for ending "the war of choice in IRAN," suggesting the money could have gone to Affordable Care Act subsidies.
Says get out of Venezuela, stop harassing Cuba, leave Greenland alone, and honor the NATO treaty.
States: "The original ICE mission is arbitrary and cruel."

H2CA03157.name: Kevin Kiley
H2CA03157.bio: U.S. Representative elected in 2022; former California State Assemblymember, Deputy Attorney General and high school English teacher.

positions.stance: Pledged to work in a bipartisan fashion to reduce the national debt and "out-of-control spending" that he says worsens inflation.
Introduced a bill to stop California from "over-taxing our gas" and supported legislation for energy independence and lower fuel costs.
Backed the bipartisan tax relief act that enhanced the Child Tax Credit and indexed it to inflation.
Supported tax relief for wildfire and storm victims, including those taxed on PG&E fire settlements.
Supported increasing and extending the Housing Tax Credit to address the shortage of affordable housing.

H6TX07177.name: Espoir Ngabo
H6TX07177.bio: Regional IT analyst at BrandSafway with nearly a decade in information technology.

positions.stance: Wants Congress to expand affordable housing, protect older apartments and invest in storm-resilient construction to lower insurance.
Supports "free, universal, single-payer care, so no Houstonian goes bankrupt staying alive."
Supports a $25 minimum wage tied to inflation.
Wants better drainage systems, restored bayous and investment in green infrastructure to protect neighborhoods before disasters.
Supports more federal support for reliable public transit to reduce congestion and connect working families to jobs.
Supports strengthening early literacy, expanding career and technical education, and investing in workforce development and lifelong learning.
Supports early childhood literacy programs, access to books, and teaching media and digital literacy so students can recognize misinformation.
Supports expanding career and technical education, apprenticeships, trade schools and employer-school partnerships.
Wants students taught how AI works and its limits, plus responsible AI use and energy-efficient, responsible data center growth.
Supports teaching budgeting, credit, taxes, banking, insurance, retirement planning and small business fundamentals.

H6FL03149.name: Mike Klein
H6FL03149.bio: West Point graduate and former Army infantry officer in Operation Desert Storm; co-founder and chairman of Warrior Centric Health.

positions.stance: Protect constitutional rights, ensure transparency, end gerrymandering, get money out of politics, and respect due process.
"Strength Through Peace": diplomacy-led global leadership, support for troops and veterans, and foreign policy in the national interest.
Energy and food security, local supply chains, small businesses, youth apprenticeships, rescuing Social Security, and education as a strategic imperative.
Supports a modern Civilian Conservation Corps, local infrastructure investment, digital skills training, and arts and culture.
"American Dream 2.0": affordable healthcare, basic income for all families, entrepreneurial freedom and fair reward for hard work.
Calls his American Prosperity Card Act his top issue, aimed at recapturing bank fees and interest "to benefit the 99% not the banks."
Wants big money out of politics, criticizing Citizens United, and to close revolving doors between government and special interests.
Supports a single-payer system, saying "There should not be a profit motive in our healthcare system."
Will fight to close tax loopholes used by institutional investors and streamline programs to make homes affordable for local families.
Supports a minimum wage tied to inflation.

H6FL04246.name: Mike Sell
H6FL04246.bio: Operational excellence and community engagement professional who has worked with healthcare and human resources industry organizations.

positions.stance: "Fund public education."
"Rein in exploitive technologies."
"Divest from overseas conflicts."
"Enact sensible gun legislation."
"Prosecute the perpetrators."

H6FL07249.name: Christopher Dennison
H6FL07249.bio: Air Force veteran, former youth football coach, and former banking collections worker.

positions.stance: Says building a data center on private property is between owners and neighbors; "The federal government has no business in that decision."
Wants to end qualified immunity so no government employee is shielded from consequences of violating someone's rights.
Says abortion is not a federal question and belongs to the states; will not vote to give Washington power over it either way.
Opposes the death penalty: "The State Should Not Decide Who Dies," citing wrongful convictions.
Wants to end foreign aid and have nations pay for U.S. troops on their soil.

H4FL11089.name: Ralph Groves
H4FL11089.bio: Retired Defense Intelligence Agency civilian analyst and retired Army major; former chairman of the Libertarian Party of Orange County.

positions.stance: Says he is "very dedicated to both Medicare and Social Security."
Favors National Guard troops being kept at home.
Will work with Vice President JD Vance to tackle Medicare fraud.
Wants presidents to commit forces overseas only for U.S. defense and for no more than 60 days without congressional authorization.
Says life should generally be promoted; abortions should be available, especially for medical purposes, and performed in hospitals.

H6FL12231.name: Branden Scrivener
H6FL12231.bio: Healthcare worker for over three years handling patient insurance authorizations; holds a bachelor's degree in human services.

positions.stance: Supports strict term limits (eight years for the House), uncapping House size, campaign finance reform, and open primaries.
Says public education funding should not be diverted to charter and other third-party school programs; teachers need support.
Says working-class Americans' interests must be prioritized over those of foreign nations or corporate capital.
Wants government access to personal data to require a warrant, and no government purchases of consumer data.
Opposes overdevelopment and "AI data centers paid for by Floridians"; supports expanding public transportation.
Says he is fighting to restore the Medicare and Medicaid funding cuts passed by Republicans.
Supports expanding Healthcare.gov with caps on premiums and deductibles tied to income and employers covering only deductibles.
Supports universal healthcare with guaranteed coverage for every American and capped, income-based costs.
Supports federally funded wind, water and solar on federal land, paid for by ending oil and fuel industry subsidies.
Supports federal investment and automaker requirements for affordable EVs, a $20,000 rebate, and charging stations on public land.

H6FL14245.name: Brian Lambert
H6FL14245.bio: Retired U.S. Navy veteran with 20 years of service.

positions.stance: "Restore fiscal discipline, balance the budget, and protect future generations from crushing debt."
"The Constitution limits the government—not the people. Every law begins there."
"Protect the freedoms guaranteed by the Bill of Rights and defend individual choice."
"Protect the right to keep and bear arms and defend the Constitution without compromise."
"America must keep its promises to the men and women who served."

H6FL06365.name: Mark Davis
H6FL06365.bio: U.S. Air Force veteran (eight years) and small business owner who spent 16 years leading operations for a large national retailer.

positions.stance: Says rents, insurance and property taxes are rising while wages stagnate, tariffs worsen costs, and policies should lift everyday Floridians.
Says immigration and crime can be addressed with smart policies and respect for liberty, without militarizing streets.
Supports universal healthcare: "We need a system that actually covers everyone without bankrupting them."
Wants a democracy "where everyone's a stakeholder, not just a chosen few."
Calls for common sense on both: "Nobody wants the government forcing birth. Nobody wants unstable people walking into schools with AR-15s."

H6FL17081.name: Michael Quirk
H6FL17081.bio: Thirty-year career in cybersecurity keeping banks, airlines and critical systems secure; Sarasota small business owner.

positions.stance: Focus on groceries, prescriptions and insurance premiums, with "no cuts to the Social Security and Medicare you earned."
Wants insurance, coastal and hurricane-evacuation failures "treated like the emergencies they are."
Pledges to apply his cybersecurity background to protecting personal data, the power grid and utility bills.
Supports open primaries, term limits, no congressional stock trading, and "no budget, no pay."
Says Congress must debate and vote before Americans fight or fund a war.

H6FL18204.name: Deva Simmons
H6FL18204.bio: Educator with more than 20 years in education in Polk County.

positions.stance: "Healthcare is a right, not a privilege"; supports lower drug costs for seniors and protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act.
Supports higher teacher pay, expanded early childhood education, more affordable college and protecting public schools from defunding.
Supports raising the minimum wage to a living wage, small businesses, clean energy jobs and workers' right to organize.
Supports protecting voting rights, fighting gerrymandering, campaign finance reform and election security.
Supports repealing the 17th Amendment so state legislatures again select U.S. senators.
Will judge bills by whether "the Constitution authorize[s] Congress to do this" and reclaim lawmaking authority from agencies.
Supports expanding the House by 100-200 members and an amendment requiring reconsideration of representation after every census.
Wants Congress to restrain spending, borrowing and monetary expansion, and supports a dollar backed by tangible monetary assets.

H6FL20119.name: Kedner Maxime
H6FL20119.bio: Pastor, founder of Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services (since 1996), and longtime WLQY radio host.

positions.stance: Will fight to bring down housing, grocery, insurance and healthcare costs and open pathways to ownership and long-term wealth.
Supports "Secure borders, fair laws, and a path forward," combining security and compassion.
"Healthcare is a right, not a luxury"; will fight to lower drug costs.
Will fight to raise school funding and teacher pay and build pathways to careers.

H6FL21109.name: Alexander Cooke
H6FL21109.bio: Former Mayor of Juno Beach and founder and CEO of Optimist Capital; previously worked on Wall Street.

positions.stance: Supports federal pressure on the property insurance crisis, property tax relief, and stopping institutional buyers from hoarding starter homes.
Wants to stop Lake Okeechobee discharges east and west, send water south through the Everglades, and defend the Indian River Lagoon.
Supports cutting federal red tape, expanding SBA-backed loans, and defending independent contractors from anti-1099 rules.
Wants to address grocery and energy inflation, cut regulatory bottlenecks, and defend Social Security and Medicare.
Refuses corporate and party-leadership PAC money; supports term limits and a ban on congressional stock trading.

H6FL24061.name: Andy Daro
H6FL24061.bio: North Bay Village commissioner (elected 2022) and founder of The Daro Team at Compass real estate.

H6FL28021.name: Eddy Rojas
H6FL28021.bio: Built and leads a Florida service company over the past 20 years.

positions.stance: Will fight to cut burdensome regulations, lower taxes on small businesses, and bring good-paying jobs back to Miami.
Supports school choice, vocational training and affordable higher education.
Will support law enforcement, secure borders, and invest in community crime-prevention programs.
Will work across the aisle to lower prescription drug costs, expand telehealth and protect Medicare.

H6NY04237.name: Blay Tarnoff
H6NY04237.bio: Computer systems analyst; Nassau County Libertarian Party chair and chair of the Libertarian National Judicial Committee.

positions.stance: Says most societal problems are caused by government and "The key to happiness and prosperity is to get government OUT."
"We must end government involvement in health care and allow free market competition" to restore affordability and quality.
Argues EPA regulation protects large polluters; says "The wealthier the population, the cleaner the environment."
Calls for ending administrative agencies' regulations, ending inflation, and ending the income tax to raise real incomes.
Opposes a Central Bank Digital Currency; says the dollar should be pegged to a digital currency that cannot be inflated.

H6NY07255.name: Priscilla Ghaznavi
H6NY07255.bio: Designer with a career across seven publicly traded companies; past president of her homeowners association.

positions.stance: Will advance policies expanding affordable housing and homeownership, with property taxes reflecting income rather than rising market values.
Says healthcare "should be a fundamental human right"; supports mental health services in schools and neighborhoods.
Supports federal investment in community services for people with autism, developmental disabilities, brain injuries and mental health challenges.
Wants district schools to lead in computer science and career readiness, with pipelines to local jobs.
Supports Web 3.0 innovation with clear guardrails for transparency, accountability and security.

H6NY12313.name: Wilneida Negron
H6NY12313.bio: Former crisis counselor who has worked for two decades across government, labor, technology and financial markets on policy.

positions.stance: "Put people in charge of AI, data, and technology" rather than corporations and insiders.
Wants a pro-worker economy that protects workers from exploitation, retaliation and abusive surveillance.
Aims to lower rent, child care, elder care and health costs; supports federal support for affordable housing preservation.
Wants to make it easier for the public to see who profits from government decisions.
Supports prevention and care, including federal transit investment to improve station conditions and safety.

H6NY12297.name: Karen Ortiz
H6NY12297.bio: Attorney and former U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission administrative judge.

positions.stance: Says Congress must impeach, convict and remove officials who violate their oath, including President Trump.
Supports Medicare for All, including abortion access, gender-affirming care, fertility treatment and dental care, not tied to employment.
Supports an arms embargo on Israel and drastically reducing the U.S. military's global footprint.
Will introduce legislation to codify civil rights protections, including for LGBTQIA+, homeless and incarcerated people.
Supports due process for all and says ICE "must be dismantled and abolished."
